children: faces renewed scrutiny after Bernstein analyst Madison Rezaei cut her price target to $51 from $74, retaining an Underperform rating on the AI infrastructure provider, according to a Thursday analyst note.
Shares fell 7% in morning trading, extending October's losses to about 32% as investors reassessed the cost of the company's expansion. The new target sits about 14% below the stock's morning price.

In the June quarter, CoreWeave generated $679 million in operating cash flow while spending $9.4 billion on capital investment. The company also recorded $640 million in second-quarter interest expense, nearly one-quarter of its $2.575 billion revenue.

Interest costs are expected to rise further, with third-quarter expense projected at $860 million to $940 million. Yields on CoreWeave's 2031 bonds have climbed above 15.7%, reflecting investor concern about financing risk.

The company is continuing to build data-center capacity for AI workloads, while its three co-founders have reportedly sold roughly $3.3 billion in shares since the March 2025 IPO, including $2.4 billion this year. Investors are watching whether future cash generation can keep pace with capital needs.

title: CoreWeave Stock Tumbles as Bernstein Cuts Target on AI Debt Fears
